_README: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the calculator's known-good numbers.
Every number here was verified by hand on 17 July 2026 against the real
Both the automated tests AND the numbers quoted in WAKING-UP-CHECKLIST.md
are checked against this one file, so the two can never drift apart.
DO NOT edit a number here to make a failing test pass. A failing test means
the calculator changed. Change a number here ONLY when you have deliberately
changed the maths and confirmed the new answer is correct. If you do change
one, run 'npm test' — it will tell you if WAKING-UP-CHECKLIST.md still
disagrees, and you must update that too.

assumptions._note: Constants the calculator is built on. Re-check these each tax year.
assumptions._universalNote: The universal 15 hours for 3- and 4-year-olds has NO income test and NO work test. Only the top-up to 30 hours is lost at the cliff.
assumptions._minIncomeNote: 16 hrs/week at the National Living Wage of £12.71 from April 2026. Recheck every April.

wakingUpCases.label: Single parent, £60,000, one 2-year-old, £800/month childcare
wakingUpCases.why: The ordinary case. A family comfortably under the £100k cliff who qualifies for everything.

wakingUpCases.label: Single parent, £130,000, one 3-year-old, £1,250/month childcare
wakingUpCases.why: Over the £100k cliff. Tax-Free Childcare and the working-parent top-up are gone, but a 3-year-old keeps the UNIVERSAL 15 hours, which has no income test. Showing £0 here told higher earners to skip £3,659 they were entitled to.

wakingUpCases.label: Single parent, exactly £100,000, one 2-year-old, £800/month childcare
wakingUpCases.why: The last penny on the good side of the cliff. Still qualifies for everything.

wakingUpCases.label: Single parent, exactly £100,001, one 2-year-old, £800/month childcare
wakingUpCases.why: One pound over. Loses all childcare support. The pension relief must NOT collapse.

extraCases.label: £60,000 income but £100,000/month childcare
extraCases.why: Nonsense input. Funded hours must stay capped at the entitlement and never balloon.

extraCases.label: £10,000,000 income, one 2-year-old, £800/month childcare
extraCases.why: Nonsense input. The recommended pension contribution must be capped at the annual allowance.

extraCases.label: £110,000 income with £1,000/month existing pension, one 2-year-old
extraCases.why: Eligibility runs on income AFTER pension. £110k minus £12k is £98k, so this family DOES qualify.

extraCases.label: Couple, £120,000 and £110,000, one 1-year-old, £1,200/month
extraCases.why: The cliff is tested per parent, not on household total. Both are over, so both lose support.

extraCases.label: £40,000, one 7-year-old, £400/month childcare
extraCases.why: Too old for funded hours, but Tax-Free Childcare still applies up to age 11.

extraCases.label: £60,000, child aged exactly 4
extraCases.why: Age 4 is the last year that qualifies for funded hours.

extraCases.label: £60,000, child aged exactly 5
extraCases.why: Age 5 is one year too old. Funded hours stop; Tax-Free Childcare continues.

extraCases.label: £130,000, one 4-year-old — universal 15 hours survive the £100k cliff
extraCases.why: The universal 15 hours for 3- and 4-year-olds has no income test whatsoever. A household far over the cliff still gets it, and must be told so.

extraCases.label: £130,000, one 2-year-old — nothing survives the cliff
extraCases.why: The universal entitlement starts at 3. A 2-year-old's funded hours are entirely working-parent hours, so over the cliff they really are £0.

extraCases.label: £10,300 income, one 3-year-old — under the minimum income test
extraCases.why: The universal 15 hours needs no work test either. A parent earning too little for the working-parent hours still gets it, though Tax-Free Childcare is correctly £0.

extraCases.label: £10,600 income, one 3-year-old — just over the minimum income test
extraCases.why: 16 hrs/week at the 2026/27 National Living Wage of £12.71 is £10,575. Using last year's £12.21 rate wrongly passed people between £10,158 and £10,575.

extraCases.label: £60,000, baby under 9 months
extraCases.why: Funded hours start at 9 months. A 3-month-old qualifies for none of them yet. Tax-Free Childcare still applies from birth.

extraCases.label: £60,000, baby aged 9-11 months
extraCases.why: The other side of the 9-month boundary. The full working-parent 30 hours begins here.

rejectedInputs.label: Partner ticked but their income left blank
